name: HandBrush
summary: The bare hand works like a paintbrush for grouping objects: sweeping the fingertip or palm strings the touched objects together into a group, drawing a loop around objects in view groups them all, and further strokes erase, split or join groups.
howItWorks: With Pico Neo3 hand tracking and six gestures. Line mode uses the fingertip (thin brush) or the palm (wide brush); objects in the swept space are selected and linked by a line in sweep order, and a confirm gesture makes them a group. Block mode draws a closed loop in view and groups the objects inside it, shown as a coloured block. Erase mode removes objects or whole groups; a stroke across one line or block splits it, and a stroke across several connects them. With 16 participants grouping objects on a plane 10 m away, it was faster and more accurate than ray, screen-rectangle and cone selection, and Split and Connect made changing groups faster.

relationships.note: Compared with the Cone method of Shi et al.
